title: fix(app-shell): the flow start node offers Object for record triggers only, and never flags its Entry condition (objectui#12780)
body:
Fixes #12780
Clause-②: no

The start node's Object and Entry condition fields were gated on trigger tokens the engine doesn't match. This PR gates every start-group field on the trigger kinds whose engine binding reads it, and pins that table so a new field can't drift. No prop, export, type or stored shape changes, so Clause-② is no.

## What the engine reads

Read at objectstack main 5c2ac83 and in the published 18.0.0-next.2 tarballs (same text). The installed `@objectstack/spec` is 18.0.0-next.2.

| start field | read by | where |
|---|---|---|
| `secret` | api | trigger-api `api-trigger.ts:250-262` |
| `objectName` | record_change | `engine.ts:3799`, `:3816` lift it into the binding; record-change trigger `:265`, `:311`, `:389` hook it |
| `objectName` on time_relative | not the sweep | `engine.ts:3840-3843` fallback only feeds `getFlowRuntimeStates` (`:4911`); the sweep parses `config.timeRelative` (`time-relative-trigger.ts:334`), whose `object` is required (`time-relative-trigger.zod.ts:137`) |
| `objectName` on schedule / api | none | the schedule and api bindings carry no object; trigger-schedule and trigger-api never read it |
| `condition` | every run, any kind or none | `engine.ts:6643-6656`, the trigger-condition gate in `execute()`, a manual run included |
| `schedule.expression` | schedule, time_relative | `schedule-trigger.ts:703`, `time-relative-trigger.ts:384` |
| `timeRelative.*` | time_relative | `time-relative-trigger.ts:334` |

## What changed

`flow-node-config.ts`, the `start` group:
- **Object:** `showWhen` keeps only the five `record-*` tokens, with `flowKind: ['record_change']` beside it. That's the gate mechanism from #12777; there's no new one. The New automation dialog reads the same `showWhen`, so it no longer asks for an object for Schedule or Webhook / API, and no longer writes `objectName` for them.
- **Object help** (EN and zh): "Object whose record changes start this flow."
- **Entry condition:** no gate at all. The engine evaluates it on every run.

A stored `objectName` on a schedule start node, such as app-todo's `task_reminder` shape, is still shown with the "Kept, not in effect" banner. Opening the node writes nothing.

## Before / after (live)

Published `@objectstack` 18.0.0-next.2 showcase, booted with `e2e/live/ci/start-backend.sh`, with this worktree's console dev server. Before = `main`'s `flow-node-config.ts` and `i18n.ts` swapped in; the restore was checked blob-equal to HEAD.

| flow, start node | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Inbound Task Webhook (stored `triggerType: 'api'`) | Object offered | Object not offered |
| Alert on Urgent Task (record-after-write), control | Object live, 0 banners | same |
| One Task Sign-off (no trigger) | Entry condition hidden | Entry condition shown |
| Scheduled Project Digest | Object hidden | same |

Screenshots and JSON: branch `claude/issue-12780-evidence`, `evidence/12780/`.

## Tests

- **`flow-node-config.startGates-12780.test.ts`, the enumeration pin.**
  - The table must name every start field, so a new field can't land without a row.
  - Each kind-gated field's `flowKind` must equal its row, and the every-run field must carry no gate.
  - Over 9 start shapes that the installed resolver is asked to classify: each field is offered empty exactly where the engine reads it, and a stored value is flagged exactly where it doesn't.
  - Every token in the Object gate must resolve to `record_change`.
- **`FlowNodeInspector.startGates-12780.test.tsx`**, through the real inspector:
  - app-todo `task_reminder`'s start config, with and without a Schedule token: banner shown, no patch on mount.
  - A time-relative start doesn't offer Object.
  - CONTROL: app-todo `task_completion` keeps Object live.
- **Old pins re-read.** Three older pins asserted the falsified premises: the API-token pin (11054), the platform-event pin (11067), and the showWhen census (34 to 33).

### Ablations

Run at `0e90d37`. Every mutation landed on disk, and every restore was blob `321335970b55` == HEAD with an empty `git diff HEAD`.

| mutant | failed (of 140) |
|---|---|
| A1: Object gate gets `schedule`, `api` back | 6 |
| A2: Object's `flowKind` removed | 1 (the declaration pin; behaviourally redundant, because `record_change` resolves only from a token) |
| A3: Entry condition gate restored | 4 |
| A4: Object's `flowKind` gets `time_relative` | 4 |

The first A2 run was a no-op: the tool refused an empty replacement. It was re-run with a marker replacement.

## Gates (local, at `9981149`)

- Build closure `@object-ui/app-shell^...`: exit 0, 29 of 47 projects.
- app-shell `type-check`: exit 0.
- vitest over the 232-file family: 2441 passed, 1 skipped.
- `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`: exit 0.
- `check:changeset-claims`, `changeset:check`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check-changeset-presence`: exit 0.
- eslint on the changed files: exit 0.
- Not run: the `packages/i18n` vitest suite (missed). The only string change is one help string, and the four i18n checks passed.

## Acceptance notes

- **Object on a time-relative start.** The card expected it to be offered. The engine's `objectName` fallback there only labels the runtime-state row; the sweep reads `config.timeRelative.object`, which is required. Offering Object would lead an author to a sweep that doesn't bind, so it is not offered. A4 pins this.
- **The examples.** app-todo's `task_reminder` and `overdue_escalation` still store a schedule `objectName`. Whether the examples drop it, or the spec refuses it, is an objectstack card under the self-split rule.
- **Advisory expression checks.** `validateFlowExpressions` uses `config.objectName` as a schema hint on any kind. This is advisory and only logs.
- **Second start node.** A second top-level start node still shows its ungated fields as live, although the engine reads only the first. This was already true before this PR.
- **Schedule cadence.** #12779 (the cadence read) is not addressed here.
